texts.preamble: Thota Karunakar And Anothers vs State Of Ap., Rep.By Its P.P on 10 October, 2018 Smt Justice T. Rajani Criminal Petition No.10172 of 2011 Order:
texts.facts: This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/A.1 and A.2 in C.C.No.536 of 2010 on the file of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Warangal District, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 16 (1-A) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, 'the Act'). 2. The allegations in the charge sheet would go to show that the date of inspection is on 08.11.2008 and the sample was lifted on the same day and sent to the chemical analyst and received by the lab on 10.11.2008 and the chemical analysis report was received on 15.12.2008 and the complaint was filed on 14.10.2010.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the right given to the petitioners under Section 13 (2) of the Act is defeated because of delay in filing the report. He further submits that the complainant did not take sufficient care to preserve the sample in order to exercise the right given to the petitioners under Section 13 (2) of the Act. 5. This Court in R. Hari Hara Reddy Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh1 held that the inordinate delay in filing the complaint would deprive the valuable right offered on the accused under Section 13(2) 2017(2) ALD (Crl.) 662 2 TR,J crlp_10172_2011 of the Act. 6. The decision of the Supreme Court in State of Haryana Vs. Unique Farmaid (P) Limilted2 is also on the same lines. Relevant portion at paragraphs 11 and 12 observed as follows: "11. Sub-section (1) of Section 30 which appears to be relevant only prescribes in effect that ignorance would be of no defence but that does not mean that if there are contraventions of other mandatory provisions of the Act, the accused have no remedy. Then in order to safeguard the right of the Thota Karunakar And Anothers vs State Of Ap., Rep. In State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd. [(1996) 11 SCC 613] this Court in somewhat similar circumstances said that the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Act deprived the accused to have sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory and adduce evidence of the report so given in his defence. We have cases under the Drugs (1999) 8 SCC 190 3 TR,J crlp_10172_2011 and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 involving the same question. In this connection reference be made to decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Brij Lal Mittal [(1998) 5 SCC 343] under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970]; Chetumal v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr. [(1981) 3 SCC 72} and Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf, [(1999)] 2 SCC 400] all under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 12.
